Hi Danielle —

Good questions; we can definitely model this. High-level approach I propose for the workshop: 

1) Workload fingerprinting: sample qps/token-length distribution from your staging traces (even aggregated histograms) so we can parameterize warm vs cold KV cache hit rates.
2) Simulation-driven slab maps: run a short simulation that sweeps (nodes per slab) x (concurrency per node) x (KV-cache-hit-rate) to produce an "absorption map" showing sustained throughput and burst headroom.
3) Egress bounding: in parallel, compute token->egress-byte conversion for your embedding/generation mix and overlay egress caps to find operationally feasible sustain/burst pairs.
4) Operational controls: recommend a minimal set of shaping & buffering knobs (client-side token windowing, L4 QoS, and our prefix-cache warm policy) to keep user-visible P99 within your SLOs while maximizing utilization.

I've attached an initial sketch of the absorption map and a first-pass egress estimate table. These are intentionally conservative — the simulation will refine the curves after we ingest your token-length histogram.

Proposed next step: 75-min working session tomorrow (Thu 6/19) 10:30-11:45am PT to run through the simulation inputs and finalize the slab allocations for pilot. Confirm if that works for you and I'll invite the right ops folks.

On Wed, Jun 18, 2025 at 11:02 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I've attached an initial sketch of the absorption map and a first-pass egress estimate table.

Thanks — adding a few concrete numbers so the team has something to react to before the workshop. These are back-of-envelope but instrument the simulation tolerances: 

- Baseline node profile: A100-40GB, single-socket, expected sustained throughput (mixed mix) 30k tokens/min per node at 95% KV-hit baseline.
- Slab sizing stage 1 (pilot low): 6 nodes per slab -> sustained 180k tokens/min (with 95% KV hit).
- Slab sizing stage 2 (pilot nominal): 8 nodes per slab -> sustained 240k tokens/min; supports short bursts to ~500k tokens/min for ~60-120s when prewarmed and with prefix cache warm.
- Egress calculation: assume 1 token ~= 0.25 bytes for pure logits stream output; for richer response/embedding mix use 0.45 bytes/token. With 2.2 Gbps egress cap the theoretical maximum is ~489k tokens/min (at 0.45 bytes/token). That means your 420k tokens/min short bursts are near the egress ceiling if responses are verbose.

Operational notes:
- If your payloads include blobs (images, base64 results), plan for higher egress headroom or client-side references to S3.
- We should model KV-cache ramp: a cold start window of ~40-90s reduces effective throughput by ~25-40% depending on request locality. That reduces safe burst throughput unless prewarming or sticky routing is used.

I've attached a tiny workbook (network-egress-estimates.xlsx) with the token->egress calculators and a column for safety margins. We'll load real histograms in the session.

—Karthik
